n: Granulosa cell tumor with Call-Exner bodies

ww.Dysgerminoma: Dysgerminoma forms sheets of large, round cells with clear cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, divided by fibrous septa full of lymphocytes. These small, dark cells with tiny follicle-like spaces point to a granulosa cell tumor.
ww.Yolk sac tumor: Yolk sac tumor shows a lace-like network of spaces and glomerulus-like Schiller-Duval bodies, with a high serum AFP, in a young patient. It lacks uniform small cells and ring-like Call-Exner spaces.
ww.High-grade serous carcinoma: High-grade serous carcinoma has papillae and slit-like glands lined by markedly atypical, pleomorphic cells, often with psammoma bodies. The monotonous small cells and tiny rosette-like spaces here are not that.
ww.Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor forms hollow or solid tubules of Sertoli cells with clusters of Leydig cells between them, and it causes virilization. Call-Exner bodies are not its pattern.

look: Solid sheets of small, uniform cells with scant cytoplasm and oval nuclei are punctuated by tiny round spaces ringed by cells and holding pink material. These are Call-Exner bodies, miniature follicles that recall the granulosa cell's normal job, and they mark a tumor that makes estrogen. Spot them first, then recall inhibin as its serum marker.
findings: Call-Exner bodies: tiny round, follicle-like spaces ringed by tumor cells and often holding pink material are scattered through the sheets, most clearly in the upper middle and center of the field; they are the classic hallmark of a granulosa cell tumor.
Diffuse sheets of small, uniform cells: monotonous round to oval nuclei with scant cytoplasm show a single population that resembles follicular granulosa cells.
Fibrovascular stroma: a band of pink fibrous tissue with thin vessels runs diagonally from the middle of the left edge down to the bottom right, separating the solid sheets of tumor into regions.

ann.l: Call-Exner body. A small follicle-like space filled with eosinophilic fluid, rimmed by granulosa cells arranged radially like a rosette; it recapitulates an immature ovarian follicle and is the classic hallmark of a granulosa cell tumor.

Diffuse sheets of granulosa cells: monotonous, crowded cells with scant cytoplasm and round-to-oval nuclei dominate the parenchyma. Some nuclei display characteristic longitudinal indentations ('coffee-bean' nuclei).
Fibrovascular stroma: a pink collagenous septal band bearing thin-walled vascular channels traverses diagonally across the field, dividing the hypercellular sheets of granulosa cells into lobules.
